newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends steady to down, fronts lose.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends steady to down, fronts lose.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended steady to lower Monday in a moderate session, with front months pressured all day by cratering physical prices from the mild weather blanketing the nation, sources said.
March slipped 7.2 cents to close at $2.313 per million British thermal units. April settled 3.2 cents lower at $2.107. Most other deferreds ended unchanged.

"There's mild weather all over the place and cash started out very soft today, but we held the daily trendline (in March). We'll have to see if there's any (downside) follow through tomorrow," said one Midwest trader.

While the market was oversold and due for a bounce, particularly in March which is down more than 30 percent since early January, few expected a rally to carry far, with eastern stocks in good shape and mild weather expected through the week.
But some said forecasts for some cold Arctic air next week could temper the bears.
Chartists now pegged next support in March at the Nov 5 low of $2.12. Resistance was seen first at today's $2.345-2.38 gap and then at $2.50, $2.70 and $2.80.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slumped almost 30 cents Monday to the mid-$2.40s. Midcon pipes were off a similar amount to about $2.30. New York city gate gas tumbled about 40 cents to the low-$3 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell one cents to $2.152. NYMEX said an estimated 22,416 Hub contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 21,451.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Monday.
On the KCBT, March finished 8.5 cents lower at $2.055, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread widened by 1.3 cents to 25.8 cents (NYMEX premium).
